subject: Tenant-level retention windows & regional storage: technical Q&A and migration plan
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice@brightbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant-level retention windows & regional storage: technical Q&A and migration plan

Hi team,

Forwarding BrightBridge's ask and a short set of questions we need to resolve before committing to a pilot: attached is the customer brief and the retention matrix they filled out. High-level asks from product / customer:
- Per-tenant configurable retention windows (TTL) for generated content and embeddings.
- Ability to pin tenant data to a primary region (US/EU/APAC) for storage residency.
- Safe migration path for existing tenants (minimal downtime, integrity guarantees).

Questions for eng:
1) Which pieces are feasible in a short deliverable (6-8 weeks) vs longer work (3+ months)?
2) Proposed API surface for tenant-config (what fields do we expose? names, default behavior).
3) Data movement strategy: in-place re-tagging vs cross-region copy + delete. Costs and risk.
4) Operational hooks: how will retention enforcement run (background job, streaming delete, realtime enforcement)?
5) Telemetry / audit primitives needed for compliance (queryable delete logs, retention versioning).

Please reply with short answers / items you need from product/legal. If we can pilot with BrightBridge, they are happy to sign an NDA and share production tokens to test.

Thanks,
Rafael
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Attachments: customer_requirements_brief.pdf, retention_matrix_v1.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice@brightbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant-level retention windows & regional storage: technical Q&A and migration plan

Rafael — thanks for laying this out. Quick take from an implementation and product-risk perspective. I sketched a rough implementation in the attached draw.io (implementation_sketch.drawio). Key points:

- Short deliverable (6-8 weeks):
  * Metadata-only tenant flags (tenant.retention_default_days, tenant.region_preference) with enforcement via a periodic deletion job. This avoids mass data movement initially.
  * API: PATCH /v1/tenants/:id/config { retention_days: number, region_preference: "us"|"eu"|"apac", legal_hold: bool }

- Longer work (3+ months):
  * True regional pinning (guaranteed at-rest placement) requires changes to snapshot/backup pipeline, cross-region replication logic, and storage class tagging. We'll need scheduler changes to prefer placement on region-specific node pools.
  * Migration path that copies data to new region with identity-preserving checksums + cutover step. This has storage and egress cost implications.

- Risks / open questions:
  * Encryption key scoping: do we need per-region CMKs or per-tenant keys? This affects compliance and KMS billing.
  * Backup retention and disaster recovery: how do we ensure backups don't inadvertently pull data into a disallowed region?
  * Billing: per-tenant storage accounting for cross-region copies.

I'm happy to scope a minimal API + enforcement job that would let BrightBridge opt into a retention policy while we iterate on actual physical residency guarantees. If product wants a firm timeline for strong regional guarantees we should lock in infra capacity and finalize KMS approach.

—Marissa
Director, Product Ops
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: implementation_sketch.drawio

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice@brightbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2027 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant-level retention windows & regional storage: technical Q&A and migration plan

Thanks — adding an engineering reality check. I pulled in infra notes below.

Feasibility breakdown:
- Metadata-first approach (6-8 wks): feasible. We'll implement tenant config + periodic deletion worker. Implementation details:
  * Store tenant retention config as part of tenant metadata in the primary metadata DB (no schema migrations required).
  * Deletion worker: ordered background queue per-tenant that deletes objects in batches with idempotent checksums. Important to surface deletion progress and failures via audit logs.

- Regional pinning (3-5+ months): higher complexity. Main items:
  * Storage tagging: object-level region tag and region-aware placement policy in the object store.
  * Scheduler: jobs to place or move data to region-specific node pools; require capacity reservations for pinned tenants.
  * KV cache / model-serving memoization: we must ensure cached outputs and intermediate artifacts obey residency (eviction or scoped caches).
  * Backups/snapshots: Must ensure snapshot scheduler is residency-aware; this may require changes to snapshot pipelines and snapshot storage classes.

Migration strategies: copy-and-verify is the safest. Steps: create a target bucket in desired region, stream copy objects with checksums, write a migration manifest, run verification pass, flip tenant pointer to new storage, then delete old copies after a quarantine period. This minimizes risk but doubles transient storage.

API surface suggestions (minimal):
- GET /v1/tenants/:id/config -> returns { retention_days, region_preference, legal_hold }
- PATCH /v1/tenants/:id/config -> allow updates, respond with migration_required: true/false
- GET /v1/tenants/:id/migrations -> list migration manifests/status
- POST /v1/tenants/:id/migrations -> start migration (body: target_region, copy_strategy)

Operational concerns:
- Legal holds: we need a non-destructive flag that prevents deletion jobs from removing data.
- Auditability: immutable deletion logs + per-object tombstone records for compliance.
- Monitoring: retention drift alerts (tenant with retention_days shorter than country requirements), copy failure rates, and per-tenant egress cost spikes.

Dependencies and follow-ups I need from Product/Legal:
- Confirmation on legal_hold semantics and retention_minimums by region (numbers).
- Decision on KMS scope (per-tenant vs per-region vs global).
- Pilot acceptance criteria from BrightBridge (what constitutes success for them).

I'll put a short RFC in the infra confluence page; link below. If product wants I can sketch a migration cost estimator we can show to customers.

-karthik
Sr. Eng Manager, Storage Systems
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Links: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/tenant-retention-design

Thanks Rafael and team — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 
- BrightBridge is comfortable with the metadata-first approach as long as there is a clear timeline for the stronger residency guarantees.
- For migration, minimizing egress cost is a priority. Do you have an estimate of transient storage / egress for a ~10TB tenant?
- We can commit to being a pilot customer if the migration can be scheduled out of business hours and recovery points are retained for 14 days during cutover.

Let us know what you need from procurement/legal to get NDA in place. Happy to jump on the meeting Rafael proposed.

Best,
Alice Chen
Head of Platform, BrightBridge
alice@brightbridge.com
